subject: Order form: invoicing entity, VAT allocation and pricing ladder decision
messages:
From: James Barrett <james@greenwave.health>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: anna.larsson@greenwave.health, procurement@greenwave.health
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 14:12:00 +0200
Subject: Order form: invoicing entity, VAT allocation and pricing ladder question

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the draft Order Form. Before we proceed to legal review we have two quick commercial questions that would help our procurement and tax teams:

1) Invoicing entity — the draft lists Redwood Inc. as the billing party. Our EU subsidiary (GreenWave AB) prefers to receive the invoice locally so VAT can be handled on their books. Can you confirm whether Redwood can issue invoices to GreenWave AB (local entity) or whether GreenWave AB should self-invoice / reverse-charge? If there are any limitations (payment entity, PO routing, banking), please call them out.

2) Pricing ladder & minimum commit phasing — the customer forecast shows a front-loaded Q3 ramp and lighter usage thereafter. Can we get an amended pricing ladder that allows a quarter-by-quarter minimum commit phase (Q3 60%, Q4 25%, Q1 15%)? That will determine whether we send a single upfront PO or staged POs.

Attached: GreenWave_PO_2025.pdf (PO stub) and Entity_Chart.xlsx (shows legal entities and VAT IDs).

Can you confirm so we can loop in our tax counsel?

Best,
James Barrett
Head of Procurement, GreenWave Health
james@greenwave.health

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: James Barrett <james@greenwave.health>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing entity, VAT allocation and pricing ladder question

James — thanks for the clear asks and for the attachments. Quick take below; looping Kim and Ben to confirm final language and pricing ladder details.

1) Invoicing entity / VAT
- We can invoice GreenWave AB directly if the contract lists the receiving entity (legal name + VAT ID) and banking/PO match the entity details.
- Operational caveat: our bookkeeping platform requires a single remit-to per invoice run; if you choose local invoicing for GreenWave AB we need to confirm how you will route payments (single or multiple POs).
- Alternative is Redwood invoices Redwood Inc. and GreenWave AB self-assesses VAT via reverse charge (common in EU). That path is simpler operationally for us but requires your tax counsel confirmation.

2) Pricing ladder / minimum commit phasing
- Staged minimum commit by quarter is acceptable; we typically document the schedule in Appendix A (pricing schedule) and allow staged invoicing tied to PO receipts.
- Need to confirm whether any discount tranches are contingent on hitting cumulative usage thresholds or discrete quarter thresholds.

Next steps I propose:
- Kim: please advise redline language for the invoicing/entity/VAT clause (we prefer to limit Redwood liability for taxes).
- Ben: please confirm whether sales can accept the quarter-by-quarter commit ladder and draft the schedule.

If helpful we can do a 20-min call Monday to finalize (I can host).

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing entity, VAT allocation and pricing ladder question

Tessa / Ben — reviewed James' note and attached a redline of the Order Form focusing on invoicing, tax allocation, and net terms. Key legal positions:

1) Tax clause (proposed language snippet): "Customer shall be responsible for all applicable taxes arising from the Agreement, excluding taxes based on Redwood's net income. If Customer requests invoices to a local subsidiary, Customer must provide legal entity name, VAT/Tax ID, and a valid PO; Customer is responsible for any VAT or withholding taxes applicable in its jurisdiction. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate local invoicing but disclaims liability for Customer's failure to self-assess or local filing obligations."

2) Invoicing entity & PO routing:
- We can accept invoicing to GreenWave AB provided the Order Form's Billing Entity section lists GreenWave AB and banking details align.
- Require a principal contact and confirmation of VAT ID up front.

3) Net terms:
- Given the billing complexity and cross-entity risk, propose Net 45 payment terms for invoices issued to non-US entities unless Finance approves Net 30 on a case-by-case basis.

Attached: OF-GW-redline.docx (redline with comments). I flagged the following to commercial: liability for taxes, evidence requirements for VAT credits, and fallback routing (invoice to Redwood Inc. if entity details not provided by start date).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: James Barrett <james@greenwave.health>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 16:40:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing entity, VAT allocation and pricing ladder question

James / Anna — thanks for the patience. I wanted to summarize positions so we can get to a decision quickly: 

A) Invoicing entity
- Sales is willing to invoice GreenWave AB directly provided you confirm the legal name, VAT ID and PO routing prior to countersignature. If for any reason the entity data isn't provided by the execution date, Redwood will invoice Redwood Inc. and we will expect GreenWave to handle reverse-charge or self-assessment.

B) VAT / withholding
- Legal's position: Customer responsible for VAT/withholding; Redwood will support by providing invoices with the requested line items and VAT ID where applicable but cannot assume tax liability.

C) Net terms
- Commercial compromise: Net 30 for standard EU commercial customers upon execution. For public sector or entities without established payment history we reserve Net 45, subject to Finance sign-off. If GreenWave AB provides a PO and VAT evidence we can escalate to Net 30.

D) Pricing ladder / minimum commit phasing
- We can accept the quarter-by-quarter minimum commit schedule you suggested (Q3 60% / Q4 25% / Q1 15%) provided the pricing schedule explicitly states discount bands apply to cumulative consumption across the 12-month period. I attached a proposed schedule (proposed-orderform-v3.pdf) that maps the ladder into Appendix A.

E) Next steps / ask list (short):
1. GreenWave to confirm invoicing entity details (legal name, VAT ID, remit-to bank details) by COB Wed 25 Jun.
2. GreenWave legal to review OF-GW-redline.docx and return comments.
3. If accepted, we will issue a DocuSign package for signature that reflects the billing entity you select.

If this looks right, happy to jump on a 20m handoff call Thursday to close operational items — Tessa can schedule.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-orderform-v3.pdf (pricing ladder mapping), OF-GW-redline.docx (legal redline)
